summary: Routing Editor async-saves create duplicate rule IDs causing SLA attribution mismatch in weekly reports
description:
Issue summary:
When multiple operators use the Routing Editor to save changes in quick succession, the backend occasionally creates two distinct template records with the same logical 'rule_id' (the editor-assigned identifier). The system-level primary key differs but the rule_id collision persists across the template-store and is visible to the reporting/analytics pipeline.

Impact:
- Weekly SLA and autoroute attribution incorrectly groups alerts under the wrong routing cohort.
- Auto-escalation rules triggered by reported SLA breaches can be misrouted to on-call groups that are not responsible for the affected customers.
- Customers on Dedicated tiers may see inaccurate SLA history in Console.

Environment:
- prod-us-east; template-service v3.7.1; routing-editor web client 1.12.0; reporting-pipeline v2.9.

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Two operators open the same routing template (different browser sessions).
2) Operator A makes a small rename and clicks Save.
3) Operator B, without refreshing, makes a concurrent change and clicks Save within ~1s.
4) Backend accepts both writes due to missing uniqueness constraint on rule_id and stores two rows with different internal ids but identical rule_id strings.
5) Reporting job aggregates by rule_id and collapses the rows; search/index picks the first row's metadata, causing misattribution in dashboards and SLA calculations.

Expected behavior:
- Server should enforce uniqueness of the logical rule_id or perform optimistic concurrency checks so concurrent edits cannot create duplicate logical identifiers. Reporting should never aggregate ambiguous identities into a single cohort.

Actual behavior:
- Duplicate logical rule_id allowed, reporting collapses duplicates and picks arbitrary metadata for attribution (first-write wins), leading to unexpected SLA attributions and misrouted escalations.

Relevant logs & traces:
- Sentry event: https://sentry.redwood-inference.com/organizations/redwood/issues/142987 (rule-store write anomalies)
- Grafana dashboard: https://grafana.redwood-inference.com/d/rt-templates/template-write-latency?orgId=1&from=now-1h
steps_to_reproduce: Open same routing template in two browser sessions
Operator B (without refresh): change priority -> Save within 1 second of A
Verify template-store contains two rows with same rule_id but different internal ids
Run reporting job or query analytics index to see collapsed attribution
investigation_notes: 2026-02-12 09:40 - Initial triage by Maya: observed weekly report spike for 'priority:enterprise' cohort with no corresponding config changes in changelog.
2026-02-13 14:05 - Replica of issue in staging by SRE: confirmed concurrent PUTs can create separate rows when DB unique index is absent.
2026-02-14 10:20 - DB schema review: migration 'template_store_v5' omitted unique constraint on 'rule_id' due to legacy compatibility flag.
2026-02-15 16:50 - Analytics pipeline note: ingestion job groups by rule_id string; when duplicates exist it chooses first row returned by index; index ordering is non-deterministic across clusters.
Hypothesis: race condition in template-service update path combined with missing DB uniqueness and eventual-indexing in analytics causes non-deterministic SLA attribution.
Observed ~12 duplicates created in the last 30 days across prod-us-east; typical window for concurrent saves is 200-800ms during edit bursts.
comments: Maya Chen (Reporter) 2026-02-12: Noticed customer CS flagged a wrong escalation; digging into template history showed duplicates.
Liam O'Connor (Assignee) 2026-02-13: Reproduced in staging and created minimal repro script. Adding DB migration to enforce uniqueness as a hotfix candidate.
SRE-Team 2026-02-14: Confirmed that add-unique-index can block writes; need safe migration plan (backfill + dedupe) before applying in prod.

Analytics 2026-02-15: We can temporarily change reporting aggregation to use internal_id instead of rule_id to avoid collapsing until data is cleaned; this will require mapping to human-friendly labels in the dashboard layer.
Product Ops 2026-02-16: Recommend UI-level guard (disable concurrent save) and a small banner telling users to refresh when others edit the same template.
Liam O'Connor 2026-02-18: Drafted migration plan and dedupe script (see PR link). Scheduling coordinated deploy with analytics and template-service teams on 2026-02-24.
Maya Chen 2026-02-20: Customer-facing note prepared for CS to acknowledge potential misattribution window; advising customers that SLA metrics may be adjusted post-cleanup.
actions_taken: Created safe dedupe migration script to merge duplicate rule_id rows into canonical internal_id
Added short-term reporting change to prefer internal_id aggregation (avoids collapsing duplicates)
Implemented server-side optimistic-lock check for template edits to surface conflicts to users
UI patch: show "stale edit" warning when last-modified timestamp drifts by >5s (deployed to canary)
Scheduled DB migration to add unique constraint with backfill on 2026-02-24 during low-traffic window
resolution_notes: Mitigation in progress: reporting aggregation temporarily switched and optimistic-lock added. Full resolution requires running the dedupe/backfill migration and adding a DB-level unique constraint. Post-migration analytics re-run will correct SLA history where attribution was incorrect. Final rollback plan prepared in the migration PR.
next_steps: Run dedupe migration on prod-us-east (Liam) - target 2026-02-24
Coordinate with Analytics to reprocess affected daily aggregates for last 30 days
Monitor weekly SLA reports for normalization for two subsequent cycles
Document editor concurrency limitations in authoring playbook and add e2e tests for concurrent saves
